name: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Galgar sends fresh recruits to gather cactus apples for his cooling treat. The work teaches them to forage and survive in Durotar's arid land.

sections.title: Surviving the Red Wastes
sections.body: Young orcs and Darkspear trolls take their first steps as defenders of the Horde in the Valley of Trials. Combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts quickly bring exhaustion and thirst. Learning to live off the land matters as much as learning to swing an axe. Cacti across the valley bear ripe, water-rich apples that offer relief from the desert sun.

sections.title: A Valley Delicacy
sections.body: Galgar tends his cooking in the training grounds, where he has made an art of foraging. His Cactus Apple Surprise is known among the valley's people for cooling a person faster than a plunge into river water. He sends eager recruits to gather prickly fruit from nearby cacti, keeping his kitchen stocked and ensuring new wanderers do not set out into Durotar hungry.

faq.answer: Galgar is an orc stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He prepares cooling provisions and treats such as Cactus Apple Surprise for recruits in the desert heat, rather than overseeing formal combat drills.

Cactus Apple Surprise is a popular local confection Galgar makes with fresh apples gathered from wild desert cacti. Trainees prize the refreshing snack for quick relief and hydration beneath Durotar's blistering sun.
Cactus apples grow in small clusters on the ground at the base of flowering cacti scattered through the Valley of Trials' red cliffs and canyons.

faq.q: Why does Galgar ask recruits to gather them?
faq.answer: The Valley of Trials is intensely hot, and Galgar cannot leave his post to search the desert himself. He offers portions of his prized treat to any passing novice willing to gather its raw ingredients from the brush.

faq.q: Does this quest connect to a larger storyline?
aliases: what comes after cactus apple surprise
faq.answer: No. The foraging task acquaints new recruits with gathering local resources as they complete their initial trials for the Horde.

faq.q: Why is foraging important in the Valley of Trials?
faq.answer: Durotar is a harsh land of arid rock and scrub. Horde leaders believe that learning to survive on its sparse natural resources prepares recruits to endure the trials of the wider world.

angles.text: Galgar's dish shows the resourcefulness needed to make nourishing food and refreshing treats from tough, prickly desert plants.
Settling Durotar meant adapting to an arid landscape. Dishes made from native cacti show the orcs' practical ability to thrive in their new home.
Every fresh recruit who enters the Valley of Trials quickly learns that enduring Durotar's punishing sun is part of training, alongside combat.
